release_admission.rule: Only an exact entry in release_ready may be published as a library.

portfolio_policy.keep_history: Retire unnecessary packs from the active portfolio and catalog; preserve source locks, reviewed records, receipts, and prior editions needed for reproduction.
portfolio_policy.product_rule: Prefer a small number of complementary, broad libraries with measured retrieval over overlapping topical fragments. Never infer freshness, rights, or quality from availability or package size. A second library over the same project universe in the same language is a duplicate and is rejected, whatever its size. All published supply is English knowledge: do not prepare a per-language or per-region edition of one project, because categories grow by subject. The exporter refuses an edition whose archive language is not English. Daily-use English categories only: general reference, practical how-to, repair and fixing, named places, history and primary texts, and travel. Programming and software-documentation lanes are out of scope.

supply_families.scope: Broad encyclopaedic reference coverage from a full, pinned English source edition. Images and third-party media are out of scope until separately reviewed. The released library may use deterministic complementary shards so each Android archive remains within its package limit.

partition_plan.rule: Create the plan only from a complete reviewed source manifest. Publish only complementary volumes whose library payload does not exceed 6 GiB (6,442,450,944 bytes).

selection_requirements: Use one immutable edition with a verified byte digest.
Preserve canonical article URLs and contributor-attribution paths.
Publish an explicit exclusion report for redirects, non-articles, malformed pages, and removed media.
If output requires more than one archive, define deterministic complementary shard boundaries and retrieval cases for cross-shard queries before packaging.
Admitting this family retires wikipedia-top1m-mini from the installable portfolio; it replaces the one English reference identity rather than adding a second overlapping English Wikipedia library.
supply_families.known_limits: A snapshot cannot provide live events or guarantee correctness of individual articles.

supply_families.scope: A complete pinned English travel-guide edition, retaining destination and contributor history paths.
selection_requirements: Resolve the existing record-count discrepancy before adopting any successor.
Do not publish a city or country subset when the same full library already supplies those records.
State that schedules, fares, safety guidance, entry rules, and opening hours may have changed.
supply_families.known_limits: No map tiles, routing, live transport, or current availability claims.

supply_families.scope: Reviewed, bounded entity facts selected from an immutable Wikidata source edition; not a live knowledge graph.
selection_requirements: Define permitted properties and data transformations before acquisition.
Retain entity identifiers and revision/snapshot identity for every record.
Exclude claims whose provenance, ranking, or temporal qualifiers cannot be rendered in the reader.
supply_families.known_limits: It cannot answer unmodeled facts, resolve every entity ambiguity, or supply current values.

supply_families.scope: Region-sharded named place snapshots with an exact query, raw snapshot digest, object URLs, source timestamp, and visible OpenStreetMap attribution. The measured first shard carries 200 named clinic, hospital, and pharmacy places from a 0.06 x 0.06 degree box around the Nairobi central business area.
selection_requirements: Release only a reviewed geographic shard; do not claim worldwide coverage from one query.
Preserve ODbL obligations and any database-derivative requirements before distribution.
Do not infer open-now state, distance, route, quality, safety, popularity, or recommendations.
Release each shard only after the extractor writes a complete reviewed manifest that names the lock digest, records the exclusion report, and carries a body digest per record.
supply_families.known_limits: Place tags and geometry are snapshots and may be incomplete, stale, or locally inconsistent. One shard covers one reviewed box; it is not a worldwide directory, and it makes no open-now, distance, route, quality, safety, popularity, or recommendation claim.

supply_families.scope: Separately reviewed official public guidance, grouped by jurisdiction and subject instead of mixing incompatible national advice into one global authority. The first edition consolidates 23 U.S. federal pages from the seven retired single-topic packs: 23 records, 211 passages, a 372,736-byte payload.
selection_requirements: Approve rights and reuse conditions for every publisher and page.
Keep jurisdiction, publication date, and local-authority limitations visible on every record.
Split a source into a new immutable edition when its advice or rights change.
Refresh a moved page set with `python -m blobs_corpus.web_pages refresh`, which keeps the reviewed selector and identity and records the changed sources in refreshed_from lineage.
supply_families.known_limits: Official guidance can still be jurisdiction-specific, time-sensitive, and unsuitable for emergency or professional advice without current local confirmation.

supply_families.scope: Everyday practical questions answered by English Stack Exchange sites outside programming: cooking, personal finance, travel, and home improvement. The admitted 2026-10.4 edition merges four pinned 2026-10 Kiwix archives into one reviewed library of 189,294 question pages, installed as 1,454,772,224 payload bytes from 567,686,098 archive bytes; 23,917 unanswered questions were excluded.

partition_plan.rule: Recompute the projected payload from the reviewed merged manifest before packaging; split into complementary volumes if it exceeds 6,442,450,944 bytes.

selection_requirements: Exclude programming and software-development sites: the owner scoped supply to daily-use knowledge, and code documentation is a separate profession-specific product decision.
Implement the reviewed multi-archive edition before packaging, so one library spans these archives with per-archive lineage instead of shipping a pack per site.
Keep post-level attribution: every record must retain its canonical question URL and the CC BY-SA 4.0 licence string.
Measure canonical URL and body-hash overlap against the repair lane; the same site cannot be published in both libraries.
supply_families.known_limits: Community answers are not professional, legal, medical, or safety advice, and a snapshot cannot show whether an accepted answer still applies to a newer product, law, or price.

supply_families.scope: Fix-it knowledge from five English Stack Exchange repair communities: vehicle mechanics, bicycles, aviation, 3D printing, and woodworking. The admitted 2026-10.4 edition keeps question pages with their answers and excludes images: 78,626 questions, 647,237,632 installed payload bytes, 256,576,414 archive bytes, records_sha256 091df84e. Review excluded member profiles, navigation listings, and tag directories; 9,749 unanswered questions are excluded. The robotics archive is not part of the lane because its question set is mostly programming documentation.
selection_requirements: Reject the iFixit archive as a supply source unless the owner accepts a non-commercial licence: iFixit content is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, and its guides depend on photographs that the text-only pipeline does not carry.
Keep only question pages (questions/<id>/<slug>); Stack Exchange ZIMs also carry member profiles, tag directories, and paged listings that are not answers.
Prefer repair communities whose questions are about physical equipment; a site dominated by software tooling belongs to no Blobs lane.
Decide whether electronics joins this lane as two volumes or is deferred, because 4.00 GB of archive projects past the 6 GiB installed-payload limit.
Do not overlap with the practical how-to lane; the exporter refuses repeated canonical URLs.
supply_families.known_limits: Repair instructions carry safety risk, model coverage is partial, and a text extraction loses the photographs and disassembly diagrams that make a guide usable.

supply_families.scope: Historical and primary texts in English: treaties, speeches, constitutions, court opinions, letters, and published works, so an answer can quote the document instead of summarising an article about it. The measured 2026-09.3 edition contains 622,014 curated documents (6,362,968,404 text characters; 6,425,153,383 UTF-8 bytes) from the pinned 3,905,588,830-byte nopic archive, published as four deterministic hash partitions of about 155,000 documents and 3.13 GB installed payload each.

partition_plan.rule: Four complementary volumes were measured from the complete reviewed manifest; the largest installed payload is 3,154,440,192 bytes, below 6,442,450,944, and the four together install 12,543,102,976 bytes. Each volume carries its own 10-case retrieval set; a cross-volume case set is retained at corpus/evaluation/cases/wikisource-en-history-cross-volume-v1.json.

selection_requirements: Keep only primary-text pages: author metadata pages, version indexes, disambiguation pages and subject portals are not supply (66,788 records excluded by policy v3).
Keep sub-page structure as the document identity, because a work spans many pages.
State that a transcription is not a critical edition and can carry source errors.
Preserve each record's canonical work URL and Wikisource revision-history path; 2,897 records have no revision id but all have a history URL.
Publish the edition only as the complete four-volume set; a single volume is a hash partition, not a topical selection.
supply_families.known_limits: Transcriptions preserve historical spelling and errors, provide no commentary or sourcing apparatus, and cannot answer questions about works that were never transcribed. 135 records whose bodies carried upstream U+FFFD are excluded. Legal, constitutional and treaty texts can be amended or superseded and are not professional advice.

supply_families.scope: Full article text of the most-read English Wikipedia selection: the Kiwix 2026-04 no-picture archive is 17,134,155,148 bytes and is planned as five deterministic complementary volumes inside a 32,731,709,440-byte total payload cap.

selection_requirements: This family is a successor to wikipedia-top1m-mini: admitting volume one retires the lead-section candidate in the same change instead of installing beside it.
Publish an explicit exclusion report and cross-volume retrieval cases before any volume enters release_ready.
Record measured per-volume install and retrieval cost on a phone, because a five-volume reference changes aggregate storage near the 48 GB safeguard.

supply_families.known_limits: Five volumes are five downloads and five installs on a phone; a snapshot cannot provide live events or guarantee article correctness. The admitted mini already replays only 7 of 12 expected titles, so full text alone is not evidence that the reference lane is dependable.

decision.reason: The 17,134,155,148-byte archive and its five-volume payload are too large for this product. The lane is withdrawn; do not acquire the archive or resume capacity planning unless the owner explicitly reopens it.

legacy_dispositions.reason: Prepared and packaged as a distinct-language travel work (4,097 guides, 54,059,008-byte payload, zero shared canonical URLs or body hashes with the English candidate), then withdrawn on 2026-10-24 by the owner decision that Blobs publishes English knowledge only. This was a portfolio-direction change, not a quality or rights failure.

Withdrawn on 2026-10-24 with the English-only decision. The defect it exposed is fixed in the curation policy and drives the English rebuild.
A 100-record English Wikipedia subset duplicates the broad reference lane and adds no separate install purpose. Preserve the old edition only for historical reproduction.

Do not distribute as a separate overlapping Wikipedia library beside the selected Top 1M reference candidate: 49,970 of 49,999 canonical article URLs (99.9%) also exist in the Top 1M edition, so the two cover the same English universe. The 990 MB reviewed records edition was removed on 2026-10-24 because its package and receipt had already been deleted and the records alone reproduced no published result. The source lock, the retired disposition, and the pinned 7-of-12 smoke report stay as the explanation. One English reference install identity only.
